name: 8-Man Indoor Football League
history: The 8MIFL is a semi-pro 8 man indoor football league launched in and completely based in Texas.

name: A-League
history: The A-League was a short league ran in 2019 with 3 teams. All games were played in the Hertz Arena.

name: All American League 2
history: AAL2 (American Arena League 2) was launched as a developmental tier of the American Arena League, created to provide a more regional, cost-controlled environment for lower-budget or emerging indoor football teams. It began operating after the main AAL struggled with team instability and the pandemic’s impact, offering a more flexible structure where teams could play shorter schedules and travel less. Over the last couple of seasons, AAL2 has functioned as the primary active league under the AAL brand, but it has still faced many of the same challenges, teams frequently folding, postponing seasons, or playing partial schedules. Despite this, AAL2 has continued producing competitive regional matchups and has acted as a landing spot for new or returning teams trying to enter the indoor football landscape. As the main AAL plans a relaunch for 2026, AAL2 remains a transitional platform, keeping the brand alive while teams stabilize and the league works toward rebuilding stronger long-term operations.

name: American Arena League
history: The American Arena League (AAL) began in 2017 with the merger of the Arena Pro Football (APF) and the Can-Am Indoor Football League, and kicked off play in 2018. The league launched with optimism and a large lineup of teams drawn from both predecessor leagues, but early seasons were marked by constant instability, including teams folding, relocating, or withdrawing mid-season. After some competitive but chaotic years, the league was hit hard by the COVID-19 pandemic, causing the entire 2020 season to be canceled and disrupting operations through 2021. In recent seasons the AAL has shifted toward a developmental structure through AAL2, operating with smaller regional schedules while attempting to rebuild stability. The league now plans a full relaunch of the primary AAL for 2026, hoping to return with stronger organization and more reliable team participation.

name: American Indoor Football
history: American Indoor Football (AIF) is a professional indoor football league in the United States, established in 2005 as the Atlantic Indoor Football League (AIFL). It underwent several rebrandings, becoming the American Indoor Football League in 2006 and the American Indoor Football Association (AIFA) from 2007 to 2010. The league experienced rapid expansion and contraction, leading to a split in 2010, with Eastern teams merging into the Southern Indoor Football League and Western teams attempting to continue as AIFA West before ceasing operations in 2011. The AIF relaunched in 2012 but ceased operations again after the 2016 season. In 2023, the league was revived with new teams, including the Cedar Rapids River Kings and Columbus Lions. However, following the 2024 season, all remaining teams departed for other leagues, leading to another cessation of AIF operations. In 2025, under new ownership, the league adopted a looser membership model, encouraging interleague play. Despite multiple revivals, the AIF has faced challenges in maintaining stability.​

name: American Indoor Football Alliance
history: The AIFA was founded in 2021 as a minor-professional indoor football league in the U.S., and began play in 2022 with several teams that broke away from the American Arena League (AAL). Its teams operated on modest budgets, and it sought to offer regional indoor football competition with reduced travel and lower overhead. The league crowned its inaugural champion in 2022, the Mississippi Raiders, and in 2023, the Columbus Lions went undefeated to win the title. By late 2023, the league’s website shut down, and most of its member teams had departed to join other leagues, indicating the AIFA had essentially folded.

name: American Professional Football League
history: The American Professional Football League (APFL) was a Midwestern indoor football league that operated from 2003 to 2013, centered mainly around Kansas, Iowa, and surrounding states. It featured a mix of fully professional and semi-pro teams, with a small group of “core” franchises playing full schedules each year while others played partial slates but could still take part in the postseason. The league was dominated in its early years by the Kansas Koyotes, who won multiple championships before teams like the Iowa Blackhawks and Sioux City Bandits rose to challenge them. Leadership was run internally by league organizers Ralph and Ted Adams, and although the league lasted a full decade, many teams eventually left to join newer, more organized indoor leagues. After the 2012 season, most remaining stable teams moved to the newly formed CPIFL, bringing the APFL to an end.

name: American West Football Conference
history: The AWFC was founded in 2018 by Platinum Events & Security, LLC (owners of the Idaho Horsemen) to fill a gap in indoor/arena football on the U.S. West Coast and reduce travel burdens for teams. It held its inaugural season in 2019 with four teams. The league faced early instability, expansion teams failed to launch, one franchise folded mid-planning, and the 2020 season was cancelled due to COVID-19. Leadership included president Chris Reynolds and commissioner Brandon Berner. By 2024, with its flagship team joining a larger indoor league, the AWFC effectively folded after several remaining franchises suspended operations.

name: Arena Football 2
history: The arenafootball2 (af2) was founded in 1999 as a developmental league for the Arena Football League (AFL), designed to bring arena football to smaller markets at a lower cost. It followed the same fast-paced, high-scoring format as the AFL but operated with lower player salaries and team budgets. The league expanded rapidly, reaching its peak with over 25 teams. However, financial struggles within the AFL led to the af2 ceasing operations after the 2009 season. Many of its teams transitioned to the newly formed Indoor Football League (IFL) or the restructured AFL in 2010.

name: Arena Football Association
history: The Arena Football Association (AFA) was a professional indoor football league operating primarily in Texas, Kansas, and Mississippi. Established in June 2021, the league began with five teams, initially referred to as the Lone Star Series. Founded by three African-American entrepreneurs, the AFA emphasized principles of diversity, equity, and inclusion, strategically placing its teams in underserved markets.

name: Arena Football League
history: The Arena Football League (AFL) was founded in 1987 by Jim Foster and became the most recognizable indoor football league, known for its fast-paced, high-scoring style played on a 50-yard field with rebound nets. It reached peak popularity in the late 1990s and early 2000s, securing national TV contracts and attracting major investors. However, financial difficulties forced the league to suspend operations in 2009. It returned in 2010 under new ownership but continued to struggle, ultimately folding in 2019.

name: Arena Football League 2024
history: In 2024, a new group attempted to revive the AFL, but the effort was short-lived, leading to the league being rebranded as Arena Football One in 2025. Despite its multiple iterations, the AFL remains the most iconic indoor football league in history.

name: Arena Football One
history: Arena Football One (AF1) was founded in 2024 as a new professional arena football league formed after the collapse of the previous Arena Football League. Eight teams from the old AFL chose to join this new organization, launching AF1’s inaugural season in 2025. Led by commissioner Jeff Fisher, with longtime indoor-football executive Jerry Kurz as CEO, the league set up headquarters in Nashville and quickly positioned itself as the next major attempt at a stable national arena-football system.

name: Arena Pro Football
history: Arena Pro Football (APF) was a short-lived indoor football league founded in 2016 to create a stable alternative after the collapse of American Indoor Football (AIF). Originally announced as the National Arena Football League, it rebranded to APF before its first season in 2017, featuring several former AIF teams along with new expansion clubs. The league struggled with scheduling issues, financial instability, and teams folding mid-season, but it completed its lone 2017 campaign with the Richmond Roughriders winning the championship. Later that year, APF merged with the Can-Am Indoor Football League to create the American Arena League (AAL), making APF one of the two foundational leagues that officially launched the AAL’s first season in 2018.

name: Arena Professional Football League
history: The APFL was an attempted league created by the Charlotte Thunder, West Michigan Ironmen and Pennsylvania Union, but never fully came to fruitation. It transitioned into the GLAF (Great Lakes Arena Football)

name: Can-Am Indoor Football League
history: The Can-Am Indoor Football League was a short-lived indoor football league founded in 2016 and operating for just the 2017 season. It was created by Tim Viens, who had previously been involved in American Indoor Football, and the league mostly featured a mix of new expansion teams and several travel teams meant to fill the schedule. The league struggled with stability from the start, multiple teams folded before or during the season, several games were canceled, and competitive balance was inconsistent. After completing its lone 2017 season, the Can-Am league merged with Arena Pro Football (APF) to form the American Arena League (AAL), making Can-Am one of the two founding pieces that launched the AAL’s first official season in 2018.

name: Champions Indoor Football
history: Champions Indoor Football (CIF) was a professional indoor football league founded in 2014 through a merger between the Champions Professional Indoor Football League (CPIFL) and the Lone Star Football League (LSFL). The league began play in 2015, featuring teams primarily in the Midwest and South, with notable franchises like the Sioux City Bandits, Omaha Beef, and Salina Liberty. Over the years, the league faced team turnover and financial challenges, leading to its eventual merger with the Arena Football League (AFL) in 2023, officially ending CIF as an independent league.

name: Champions Professional Indoor Football League
history: The Champions Professional Indoor Football League (CPIFL) was a minor indoor football league that operated in the Midwestern United States. Founded in 2012, the league commenced play in 2013 with teams such as the Sioux City Bandits, Omaha Beef, and Wichita Wild. The CPIFL aimed to consolidate regional indoor football teams to enhance competition and operational stability. After two seasons, the league merged with the Lone Star Football League (LSFL) in August 2014 to form Champions Indoor Football (CIF), expanding the reach and competitiveness of indoor football in the region.

name: Championship Football Assoication
history: The CFA is an upcoming indoor football league scheduled to begin play in 2026. The league will feature a nine-man format rather than the traditional eight-man game and will utilize sidelines instead of dasher boards.

name: China Arena Football League
history: The China Arena Football League was a professional arena football league in the People’s Republic of China, founded in 2012 and officially launched in 2016. The league was created by Martin E. Judge Jr. and his company, AFL Global, and carried the ambition of introducing the indoor/arena version of American football to China. In its inaugural season, the CAFL featured six teams with mixed-roster formulas (including both Chinese players and American/international imports) and held its first “China Bowl” championship in November 2016, won by the Beijing Lions. The league attempted a second season in 2019 on a shortened schedule (four teams, few games) and then faded, with its online presence disappearing and no further seasons confirmed.

name: Continental Indoor Football League
history: The Continental Indoor Football League (CIFL) was an indoor football league operating primarily in the Midwestern United States from 2006 to 2014. It was established as the Great Lakes Indoor Football League (GLIFL) in 2005 by Jeff Spitaleri, his brother Eric, and Cory Trapp, all hailing from Canton, Ohio. The league aimed to provide a platform for indoor football teams in the Great Lakes region. In 2007, reflecting its expansion beyond the Great Lakes area, the league rebranded as the CIFL. Throughout its existence, the CIFL faced challenges common to many indoor football leagues, including team instability and financial difficulties, leading to its cessation of operations after the 2014 season.

name: Covid League
history: The COVID league was a short-lived league run in 2020 during COVID, made up of 3 teams based in South Carolina and Georgia. Only 8 games were played between June and September, with the Carolina Predators winning the championship.

name: Dallas Indoor Football League
history: The Dallas Indoor Football League was a small indoor league based in Dallas, Texas, in 2021. There were 6 teams, and they played 7 weeks before quietly shutting down midseason.

name: Dev Arena Football
history: The Dev Arena Football (DEVAF) was a small league comprised of indoor and semi-pro teams that played in 2021. Teams were mainly based around Tennessee, South Carolina, and Georgia. They played one season and quietly disappeared.

name: Eastern Arena Football League
history: The Eastern Arena Football League was an indoor/semi-pro league based around the East Coast of the USA, but had teams as far as Illinois. They started in April of 2021, brought in 7 teams, and planned for a September start. But no schedule would be posted, and the league quietly folded.

name: Eastern Indoor Football League
history: The Eastern Indoor Football League (EIFL) was a small indoor football league covering the Mid-Atlantic and Northeastern U.S. that began play in 2007 with four teams. It was marred almost immediately by instability; three other announced franchises (Baltimore Blackbirds, Bay Shore Brawlers, Pittsburgh Ironmen) left the league before the first games. Early in the season, a serious player injury revealed the league lacked proper liability insurance, leading to cancelled games, venues being padlocked, and the actual schedule collapsing. By late February 2007, the league had dwindled to only two active teams and effectively folded; the HitMen were declared champions by default based on having the best record when operations ceased.

name: Eight-Man Extreme Football League
history: The Eight-Man Extreme Football League (EXFL) is a small running league operating in the East of the USA. Playing arena-style football outdoors. The league has been going on since 2017. The league faced a setback in 2025, when multiple teams dropped out before and during the season, but the EXFL is reloading for 2026.

name: Elite Indoor Football
history: The Elite Indoor Football (EIF) was an indoor football league, primarily comprising small indoor/semi-pro teams that lacked a league. They also played games against teams in other leagues to fill schedules. Ran for 6 seasons before quietly closing down before 2025.

name: Entertainment Football Association
history: Entertainment Football Association (ENTFLA) is an indoor American football league in the United States, and will launch in 2025. It will follow a seven-on-seven format with four teams along the Eastern Seaboard of the United States.

name: Fan Controlled Football League
history: Fan Controlled Football (FCF) is an indoor, seven-on-seven football league launched in 2021 with the unique concept of letting fans make real-time decisions for their teams, including calling plays and drafting players through an app. Games were played in a single arena with fast-paced rules tailored for streaming, and the league leaned heavily into a blend of traditional sports and esports-style interactivity. FCF began with four teams and expanded to eight in 2022, attracting celebrity involvement and strong online engagement. Despite completing two seasons, the league paused operations after 2022 to restructure and shift toward licensing its fan-control technology, leaving its long-term future uncertain.

name: Federated Arena League
history: The Federated Arena League (FAL) was a “faith-based league” that played in 2022, mainly in the Southeast of the USA. The FAL ran a successful season in 2022, but did not return for a 2023 season, despite teams being announced for the upcoming season.

name: Great Lakes Arena Football
history: The GLAF was a regional indoor football league based in the Great Lakes region of the United States, founded in 2023 and folded (or became dormant) in 2025. It was created to offer a “bus league” style format (limited travel, more localized teams) with the headquarters and control tied heavily to one of its member teams, the West Michigan Ironmen. After the 2024 season, many of the teams departed for other leagues, and GLAF’s operations went dormant.

name: Greater Toronto Indoor Football League
history: The Greater Toronto Indoor Football League (GTIFL) is an amateur indoor football league established in November 2023, aiming to grow the sport within Canada. Games are played at the Toronto Rock Athletic Centre in Oakville, Ontario, providing a premier venue for competition. The GTIFL has quickly developed a loyal fan base and continues to expand, offering a structured yet exciting platform for players and fans of indoor football in Canada.

name: Greatest Indoor Arena Football League
history: The GIAFL is a new indoor football league that launched in 2025. Based in Michigan, the league successfully completed its inaugural season in December 2025.

name: GridIron Indoor Football League
history: The GridIron Indoor Football League (GIFL) is a winter indoor football league based in the Southeastern USA. The GIFL has been running well since 2023 and has produced numerous players promoted to higher leagues. The league is looking forward to its 2026 season, with 6 teams, including the champions of the GIFL and EXFL.

name: Independent Indoor Football Alliance
history: The Independent Indoor Football Alliance (IIFA) was a Texas-based indoor football league founded in 2008, with its inaugural season played in the same year. It operated mostly in the Dallas–Fort Worth and East Texas region and featured several small-market teams. The league ran abbreviated seasons; 2009 saw many forfeits and teams dropping out, and it tried to improve stability in 2010 and 2011 by tightening standards and partnering with independent teams. The IIFA folded in 2012.

name: Indoor Championship Football League
history: The ICFL was a semi-pro / developmental indoor football league that appears to have operated in the early 2010s, centered in the Mid-Atlantic. The league partnered with the MIAFL and never ran its own season again.

name: Indoor Football Association
history: The Indoor Football Association (IFA) was an indoor football league based in the Midwest. It ran from 2017-2020 when COVID stopped play after Week 3. Despite numerous attempts, the league never returned to play.

name: Indoor Football League
history: The Indoor Football League (IFL) was established in 2008 through the merger of the Intense Football League and United Indoor Football.The league has maintained continuous operation under the same name and corporate structure, making it the longest-running active professional indoor football league in the United States. Following the closure of the original Arena Football League in 2019, the IFL became the oldest active professional indoor football league in North America, with roots tracing back to 2003.

name: Indoor Football League 1999-2000
history: The original IFL (not to be confused with the modern IFL founded in 2008) was a short-lived professional indoor league featuring teams primarily in the Midwest. It offered a more cost-conscious model and helped establish future indoor platforms before folding and contributing teams to other leagues.

name: Indoor Gridiron League
history: The Indoor Gridiron League (IGL) was launched in the early 2010s as a semi-professional indoor football league with roots in the Philadelphia region. More than 45 players from the league secured professional contracts within its first few seasons, and the league had a formal relationship with the Philadelphia Soul of the original Arena Football League, positioning itself as a feeder league.

name: Indoor Professional Football League
history: The Indoor Professional Football League (IPFL) was established in 1999 as a successor to the Professional Indoor Football League (PIFL). The league faced challenges during its three-year tenure and ultimately dissolved after the 2001 season. Subsequently, several of its more successful teams transitioned to the National Indoor Football League (NIFL).

name: Intense Football League
history: The Intense Football League was a professional indoor football minor league primarily based in Texas, founded in 2003 and beginning play in 2004. It operated until the end of the 2008 season, when it merged with the United Indoor Football (UIF) to form the current Indoor Football League (also abbreviated IFL) beginning in 2009.

name: International Arena Football League
history: The International Arena Football League was launched with the concept of operating an indoor-football competition across the US-Mexico border. Formed with plans for multiple teams in both countries, the league attempted to establish itself as an international platform for arena football development and cross-border play. Although announced teams were promoted and partial scheduling occurred, the league struggled with stability and execution, with several organizations never reaching full competitive operation. The IAFL ultimately remained short-lived, remembered mostly as an ambitious but incomplete attempt to expand arena football internationally.

name: International Arena League
history: The International Arena League (IAL) is a planned 8-on-8 arena football league aiming to launch in spring 2026, presenting itself as a faster, high-scoring twist on traditional indoor football. Headquartered in Las Vegas, the league intends to field teams across both North America and Europe, positioning itself as the first arena-football league with a true international footprint.

name: Lingerie Football League Canada
history: LFL Canada was a short-lived offshoot of the Legends Football League that launched in 2013 as the league’s first international expansion. It was intended to operate on a fall schedule opposite the U.S. LFL season. Although the league generated early interest, it faced major operational problems, including venue issues, player disputes, and logistical failures. The 2013 season was ultimately canceled just before kickoff, and LFL Canada never returned to play.

name: Lone Star Football League
history: The Lone Star Football League (LSFL) was a professional indoor football league that operated from 2012 to 2014, with all its teams based in Texas. The league was formed by teams transitioning from other leagues, including the Southern Indoor Football League and the Indoor Football League. Notable teams included the Amarillo Venom, who secured two championships, and the San Angelo Bandits, who clinched the final title in 2014. Following the 2014 season, the LSFL merged with the Champions Professional Indoor Football League to establish Champions Indoor Football, aiming to strengthen the indoor football landscape in the region. In 2025, Texas native and coach Tom Lewis, announced on his personal Facebook page that he plans on relaunching the LSFL, but nothing has come it yet

name: Major Indoor Football
history: A long-running semi-pro indoor football league active through the 2010s and early 2020s. It operated as a developmental circuit with flexible scheduling and small-budget teams before fading out around 2022.

name: Mesquite Indoor Football League
history: A very small, short-lived indoor football league based in Mesquite, Texas, operating around 2016–2017. It consisted of local or semi-pro teams playing in Mesquite Arena.

name: Mid West United Football League
history: The Mid-West United Football league (MWUF) was formed in 2021 when a group of 4 teams came together looking to build an old school league. The league is based off of teams trying to help each other out compared to recruiting each others players and ruining each other rosters. The league is looking to be competitive but also to work together so all teams thrive. The league is also not trying to make a profit from the teams. They will divide up the cost of running the league by the amount of teams that are in the league versus having a flat fee and have an outstanding balance in the leagues checking account year after year. The MWUF is looking to become a league that is successful together compared to seeing teams struggle year in and year out due to teams stealing their players.

name: Mid-Atlantic Indoor Football League
history: The Mid-Atlantic Indoor Football League (MAIFL) was a small regional indoor football league that operated in the late 2010s, built around teams from the Maryland & Virginia area. It functioned as a semi-pro, developmental “bus-league,” relying heavily on local recruiting, tryouts, and community engagement rather than large budgets or major arenas. By around 2020, the MAIFL had largely wound down as many of its teams and personnel moved into other leagues, including the American Arena League, effectively bringing the MAIFL era to an end.

name: Midwest Arena Football League
history: The Midwest Arena Football League (MAFL) is a regional developmental indoor football league based in the Midwest, created to provide players, coaches, and staff a competitive platform to gain experience in arena-style football. Although small in scale, the MAFL aims to offer a structured environment for athletes looking to advance into higher-level indoor or outdoor football leagues.

name: Midwest Professional Indoor Football
history: A lower-tier Midwestern indoor league built around semi-pro teams and player development. Teams came and went quickly, and the league never expanded beyond a small regional footprint before shutting down.

name: Minnesota Indoor Football League
history: A small indoor football league based in Minnesota.

name: National Arena League
history: The National Arena League (NAL) is a professional indoor football league that began play in 2017. It was created to provide a competitive arena-style football experience and has undergone various expansions and team changes over the years. The league has maintained a strong presence in indoor football despite fluctuations in membership, with teams joining and leaving for other leagues.

name: National Indoor Football
history: Originally, the Impact Developmental Football League, the NIF, is a small league started in 2020. They played 4 seasons, with 2020 getting cancelled due to COVID. In 2024, they didn't play any games, with their league up in the air. In 2025, they joined the NFA (National Football Association). The NFA hosts many types of football, including men's, women's, youth, and indoor. The NIF is planned to start up again in 2026, with 3 teams confirmed so far.

name: National Indoor Football League
history: The National Indoor Football League (NIFL) was a professional indoor football league in the United States that operated from 2001 to 2007. Founded by Carolyn Shiver and based in Lafayette, Louisiana, the NIFL aimed to bring indoor football to markets not served by the Arena Football League or its developmental league, AF2. At its peak, the league featured 22 teams. However, by 2007, the league faced significant challenges, including teams folding or defecting to other leagues, leading to its dissolution.

name: New England Arena League
history: A regional indoor league centered in the New England area. The NEAL aimed to develop players and provide affordable arena-style football entertainment locally, typically featuring semi-pro organizations with strong community ties.

name: NorCal 8-Man Indoor Football League
history: A California-based 8-man indoor football league focusing on local talent, semi-pro teams, and fast-paced gameplay adapted for smaller fields and rosters. The league prioritized accessibility and low operating costs compared to traditional 11-man arena leagues.

name: North American Indoor Football
history: The NAIF was a short-lived indoor league based around the southern US, but had teams as far north as Colorado. The X-League and NAIF had a planned merger in 2015, but cancelled it after 10 days. The NAIF played one more season in 2016, but quietly disappeared afterwards.

name: Professional Arena Independent Association
history: The PAIA is a newer indoor league started in 2025, made up of a mix of teams from other leagues and new teams. Based mainly in the Eastern US, they ran a successful 2025 season with the Peach State Cats taking the championships.

name: Professional Indoor Football League
history: The Professional Indoor Football League (PIFL) was a U.S. professional indoor football league that operated from 2012 until 2015. It launched in 2012 with six teams, mostly former members of the Southern Indoor Football League, plus the expansion Knoxville NightHawks, and quickly became a hub for small-market, regional indoor football. Over the next few seasons, it expanded and contracted, adding teams like the Lehigh Valley Steelhawks and the Nashville Venom while losing others, before ultimately discontinuing operations in September 2015 after multiple franchises folded. The final champion was the Columbus Lions, and following the collapse, many remaining clubs moved on to other leagues, like the Steelhawks and Lions, who became founding members of the National Arena League.

name: Professional Indoor Football League (1998)
history: The Professional Indoor Football League (PIFL) was a short-lived professional indoor football league founded in 1997, completing its only season in 1998 with eight teams across the United States. Created as an alternative to the Arena Football League, the PIFL adopted similar indoor-style rules but without the AFL’s rebound-net system due to patent restrictions. The league suffered from significant financial issues, including missed payrolls, team instability, and mid-season forfeits, which led to the collapse of multiple franchises. Following the season, the league effectively dissolved, with two teams departing to form the original Indoor Football League (1999–2000), while the remaining members reorganized under the new name Indoor Professional Football League (IPFL), marking the end of the PIFL brand.

name: Southern Indoor Football League
history: The Southern Indoor Football League (SIFL) was an indoor football league that operated in the Southern and Eastern United States from 2009 to 2011. Founded by Thom Hager, the league began with five teams, including the Louisiana Swashbucklers and Austin Turfcats. Over its brief existence, the SIFL expanded rapidly, reaching a peak of 16 teams in 2011. However, challenges such as team instability and financial difficulties led to the league's dissolution after the 2011 season, with many teams transitioning to other leagues or ceasing operations altogether. ​

name: Spring Indoor Football
history: The SIF (Spring Indoor Football) was a short-lived league based in and around Ohio. The SIF played a 2024 season, finishing with the Ohio Legends winning over the Ohio Boom. The league would not return for a 2025 season, and teams disappeared into other leagues.

name: Supreme Indoor Football
history: Supreme Indoor Football (SIF) was a short-lived U.S. professional indoor football league founded in 2015 by the ownership of the Cape Fear Heroes. The league originally intended to launch as part of an Indoor Football Alliance with the returning Continental Indoor Football League, but organizational plans fell apart, delaying operations. SIF eventually kicked off in 2017 with a small lineup of teams, including the Cape Fear Heroes, Cap City Bulls, Triangle Torch, and Upstate Dragons. The Heroes won the league’s only championship that season, defeating the Torch in the title game. Following the 2017 season, most clubs left to join the newly formed American Arena League, leading to the rapid collapse and quiet dissolution of Supreme Indoor Football.

name: Texas Indoor Gridiron League
history: A short-lived Texas-centered indoor football league emphasizing regional competition and reduced travel.

name: The Arena League
history: The Arena League is a new U.S. indoor American football league that launched in 2024, initially playing six-on-six football with four teams. By its second season, it had expanded to six teams and moved to a more traditional seven-on-seven indoor format. League games are held on a 50-yard arena-sized field, use 15-player rosters operating under a one-platoon system (players play both offense and defense), and feature rules like a double forward pass and a “quarterback throwoff” instead of kickoffs or punts. The league’s championship game is branded as “ArenaMania,” with the Duluth Harbor Monsters currently holding the championship title. The Arena League aims to grow by adding expansion teams for 2026, with ambitions for further expansion in the coming seasons.

name: The League
history: The Sportz League, officially branded simply as The League, is a year-round multi-sports competition headquartered in Louisville, Kentucky, operated by Elite Sports & Entertainment Group. It brings together athletes, teams, and fans across a variety of sports with a focus on innovative fan engagement, player development, and modern technology such as instant replays and live-game streaming. Originally centered around seasonal sports like baseball and basketball, The Sportz League expanded its offerings to include arena football in the fall of 2025, marking a significant milestone in its evolution as a multi-sport organization. This new football initiative added fast-paced, competitive action to the league’s calendar and broadened its appeal to football fans alongside its existing sports portfolio.

name: Ultimate Indoor Football League
history: The Ultimate Indoor Football League (UIFL) was a professional indoor football league that began its inaugural season on February 18, 2011. Co-founded by Michael Taylor and Andrew Haines, the league aimed to provide a platform for indoor football teams primarily in the Appalachian region.  After the 2014 season, the UIFL merged with X-League Indoor Football, concluding its independent operations. ​

name: United Arena League
history: The United Arena League was an indoor football league started in 2019, with its first season scheduled for 2020. COVID would delay that to 2021, and on May 8th, the first UAL season started. It would end with a championship game being played on July 17th with the Georgia-Lina Lions taking the inaugural championship. Afterwards, no posts would come on the UAL Facebook, and it is assumed that they quietly folded.

name: United Indoor Football
history: United Indoor Football (UIF) was an indoor American football league that operated in the United States from 2005 to 2008. It was established by ten teams, primarily originating from the National Indoor Football League (NIFL), with the league's headquarters based in Omaha, Nebraska. After four seasons, UIF merged with the Intense Football League (IFL) in 2008 to form the current Indoor Football League, concluding UIF's independent operations. ​

name: United Indoor Football Association
history: The United Indoor Football Association (UIFA) is a professional indoor football league dedicated to delivering fast-paced, high-energy action to fans. The league's mission centers on bringing fans closer to the game through thrilling competition and active community engagement. UIFA emphasizes top-tier athleticism, intense matchups, and family-friendly entertainment, all within an indoor setting. The league is committed to redefining indoor football and inspiring future athletes

name: United States Arena League
history: The USAL is a relatively new indoor football league, established in 2025. 8 teams played in the debut season with the Indiapnopilis Enforcers winning the championship. Not much has been posted about the future of this league.

name: United States Indoor Football
history: The Savannah Coastal Outlaws established an amateur developmental league called United States Indoor Football to operate out of the Civic Center; the league played for two weeks in 2017 before disbanding.

name: Winter Indoor Football
history: The WIF is a Midwest-based league, started in 2024. They just finished their second season in 2025, with the Pittsburgh Outlaws going back-to-back, winning their 2nd championship.

name: Women's Arena Football League
history: The Women’s Arena Football League was an 8-on-8 full-contact indoor American football league based in Houston, Texas, founded in 2011 and beginning play in 2012. It operated in the spring and summer months across various U.S. arenas and offered a more traditional athletic-gear presentation compared with lingerie-style alternatives, intending to emphasize sport and professionalism over spectacle. The league started with six teams and, at its peak, counted eight clubs playing under slightly modified indoor-football rules (notably without goalposts or rebound nets). After its inaugural season, the WAFL went dormant following 2013, but never returned.

name: World Indoor Football League
history: The World Indoor Football League was a U.S. indoor football league founded in 2007 as a breakaway from the American Indoor Football League. It operated only for the 2007 season, fielding four teams, the Augusta Spartans, Columbus Lions, Daytona Beach Thunder, and Osceola Ghostriders, after several announced teams folded or never launched. The Spartans captured the lone championship, defeating the Lions 63–60 in the only “World Indoor Bowl.” The league was plagued by instability, tragedy (including the death of a player mid-season), and departures; by the end of 2007, the remaining teams had all moved on to other leagues or folded, rendering WIFL a one-season league.

name: X League
history: The X League is a U.S. women’s semi-professional indoor/tackle football league, originally founded in 2009 under the name Lingerie Football League (LFL), then rebranded as Legends Football League in 2013, before reshaping into its current form in 2019. After a pandemic-related hiatus (no 2020 or 2021 seasons), the league relaunched and held its first full season as X League in 2022 — with eight teams and the championship “X Cup,” won by the Chicago Blitz. Under the ownership of Hall-of-Famer Mike Ditka (joined 2021) and a rebranding effort, the X League presents women’s football as a full-contact, 7-on-7 (or 50-yard field) indoor sport. It has announced plans to return in a hybrid tackle-and-flag format by 2026 and to expand operations, positioning itself as a leading women’s arena-football platform in North America. name: X-League Indoor Football
history: The X-League Indoor Football (X-League) was a professional indoor football league in the United States that operated from 2014 to 2015. Co-founded by Michael Mink and Kacee Smith, the league aimed to innovate the indoor football scene with unique rules and a distinctive scoring system. The X-League allowed two-back offensive formations and implemented defensive flexibility uncommon in other indoor leagues. Notably, it introduced the "X-Dash" to determine possession at the start of each half, awarding two points to the winner, and assigned additional points for defensive turnovers. Despite its innovative approach, the X-League faced challenges and ultimately disbanded after the 2015 season. ​
